title: Deep Fat Fryer & Hot Oil Safety
blurb: Keeping water out of hot oil, handling the fryer safely and putting out a fryer fire with a fire blanket.
siteNotes: Where the fire blanket and nearest extinguishers are in each kitchen
The venue's fryer cleaning and oil-filtering routine and who does it
The fire alarm call points and evacuation route from the kitchen

cards.title: Deep Fat Fryer & Hot Oil Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why water and hot oil are so dangerous
- use and clean a fryer safely
- respond to a fryer fire correctly

cards.title: One of the most dangerous pieces of kit
cards.body:
The oil runs at around 180°C, hot enough to cause a severe, deep burn instantly. If it catches fire, it is a fast, frightening blaze.

Almost every fryer injury and fire is preventable with care and the right habits.

items.label: Roughly how hot the oil runs

cards.title: Water and hot oil are a deadly combination
cards.body: Even a small amount of water hitting hot oil makes it spit violently and can trigger an explosion of hot oil and steam.

items.title: Dry food
items.text: Food going in should be as dry as possible.

items.title: Lower gently
items.text: Lower baskets in, do not drop them.

items.title: Keep water away
items.text: Never let water near the oil.

cards.title: Do not overfill, keep clear
cards.body: Do not overfill the fryer with oil or food, and keep the surrounding area clear.

left.title: Do
items: Keep the area around it clear

cards.title: Never move or clean it hot
cards.body:
Never, ever try to move a fryer full of hot oil. Wait until it has fully cooled before draining, filtering or cleaning it.

> Cleaning a fryer while the oil is still hot is a classic cause of serious burns.

cards.title: Do not throw water on it
cards.body: If a fryer or oil catches fire, do NOT throw water on it. That will make it explode.

items.title: Turn off heat
items.text: Only if you can do so safely.

cards.title: Know where the fire blanket is
cards.body: Know where the fire blanket is before you ever need it.

items.title: Fire blanket
items.text: Know where it is, before a fire.

items.title: Alarm
items.text: Raise it if it is not controllable.
Call it if it is not controlled.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Oil runs at around 180°C, so a burn is instant and deep
- Keep water away from hot oil and keep food dry
- Lower baskets gently, never overfill, keep the area clear
- Never move, clean or drain a fryer while the oil is hot
- Fire: no water, turn off heat, fire blanket, alarm, evacuate, 999

cards.q: Deep fryer oil runs at roughly:
cards.why: The oil runs at around 180°C, hot enough to cause a severe, deep burn instantly.

cards.q: You should never throw water on an oil fire.
cards.why: Water on burning oil makes it explode.

cards.q: A cook is about to put damp food into the fryer. Why should food be as dry as possible?
options: Water hitting hot oil makes it spit and explode
Wet food makes the oil colder and slower
Wet food spreads germs through the oil
Wet food makes the basket heavier to lower
cards.why: Even a small amount of water hitting hot oil makes it spit violently and can cause an explosion of hot oil and steam.

cards.q: It is fine to clean the fryer while the oil is still hot.
cards.why: Wait until it has fully cooled. Cleaning while hot is a classic cause of serious burns.

cards.q: The fryer oil has caught fire. How do you put it out?
options: Turn off the heat and smother it with a fire blanket
Throw water on it to cool it quickly
Fan it to blow the flames out
Carry the fryer outside to the yard
cards.why: Turn off the heat if safe, and smother the flames with a fire blanket. Never water, and never move a fryer of hot oil.

cards.q: You should never move a fryer full of hot oil.
cards.why: Wait until it has fully cooled before draining, filtering or cleaning it.

cards.q: Before you ever need it, what must you know the location of for a fryer fire?
options: The nearest tap
The first aid box
The bin store
The fire blanket
cards.why: Know where the fire blanket is before you ever need it.

cards.q: How should baskets be lowered into the oil?
options: Dropped in quickly to save time
From a height to avoid splashing
Gently
Fast, then stepping back
cards.why: Lower baskets in gently rather than dropping them.

cards.q: Overfilling the fryer with oil or food is safe.
cards.why: Do not overfill the fryer with oil or food.

cards.q: Hot oil can cause a severe, deep burn almost instantly.
cards.why: At around 180°C, the oil causes a severe, deep burn instantly.
